t: You're standing where the Hotel Cecil once stood, between the Strand and the Thames Embankment. It was a vast hotel, built between 1890 and 1896 and named after Cecil House, the Cecil family mansion that occupied the site in the seventeenth century. It was largely demolished in 1930, and Shell Mex House, now called Eighty Strand, rose in its place. Alexander Michie died at the hotel in 1902. He was a Scottish writer and businessman who worked in Hong Kong and Qing China, and wrote about travelling overland from Peking to Saint Petersburg.
